headline: Common Kitchen Island Planning Mistakes That Disrupt Your Kitchen Work Flow
articleBody:
A custom kitchen island adds remarkable storage, meal prep space, and casual dining to your home, but small oversights during planning can create daily frustrations. Here are the most common kitchen island installation mistakes homeowners make and how you can avoid them.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. Squeezing clearances too tight. Installing an oversized island that leaves less than 36 inches of walkway makes the entire kitchen feel congested. Maintain 42 to 48 inches between the island and major appliances so doors open freely.

2. Neglecting countertop overhang support. Heavy quartz or granite overhangs extending past 10 to 12 inches for barstool seating require hidden steel support brackets or legs. Skipping support risks cracking the slab under pressure.

3. Forgetting electrical outlets. Building codes often require permanent islands to include electrical receptacles, and daily convenience demands outlets for blenders and mixers. Plan electrical conduit routing before installing flooring or anchoring cabinets.

4. Overlooking stool push-back space. Many homeowners measure the island countertop but forget that guests seated on barstools need room behind them. Ensure you leave adequate passage space behind occupied chairs.

5. Ignoring floor level variations. Kitchen floors are rarely perfectly flat. Setting base cabinets directly on an uneven floor without proper shimming and leveling leads to cracked countertops and misaligned cabinet doors.
